meta.inflation_note: Birleşik Krallık şirketleri enflasyon muhasebesi uygulamaz. Bu yüzden bütün şirketlerin özsermaye kârlılığı yıl sonu tüketici enflasyonuyla düzeltildi: 2021 için %5,4, 2022 için %10,5, 2023 için %4,0, 2024 için %2,5, 2025 için %3,4. Son 12 ay için en son açıklanan yıllık oran (Eylül 2026, %3,5) kullanıldı.
data_notes: Fiyat, piyasa değeri, F/K ve PD/DD: TradingView tarayıcısı, 12 Kasım 2026. Fiyatlar peni (GBX), piyasa değerleri milyon sterlin olarak yazılır. Evren 1.071 paydır: 1.034'ü Londra Borsası'nda (ana pazar ve AIM), 37'si Aquis Borsası'nda. Depo sertifikaları, ana kotasyonu başka ülkede olan paylar ve kapalı uçlu fonların çoğu evrende yoktur; evrendeki 30 yatırım ortaklığı 1. surda dışarıda kalır.

Karşılaştırma: Londra Borsası'nın kendi güncel listesi bu çalıştırmada açılamadı. İkincil kaynaklara göre Londra Borsası'nda Mayıs 2026'da fonlar dahil 1.534 şirket vardı (Fortune, borsa verisine dayanarak). Finansal Davranış Otoritesi'ne (FCA) göre Haziran 2026'da ana pazarda 512 ticari şirketin payı kotaydı; AIM'de 2025 sonunda 619 şirket vardı. Fon dışı şirketlerde evren bu toplamın (yaklaşık 1.130) yaklaşık %11 altında. Aquis'te 80 kadar şirket var; evrende 37'si bulunuyor.

Üçüncü kaynakla düzeltilenler (13 Kasım 2026). IG Design Group: kaynak F/K'yı 26,3 gösteriyordu; şirketin 31 Mart 2026'da biten yıl sonuçlarında ana ortaklığa düşen sonuç 112,3 milyon sterlin zarar (süren faaliyetler 5,4 milyon kâr, durdurulan faaliyetler 117,7 milyon zarar). Şirket 'zarar' olarak işaretlendi. Softcat: kaynağın PD/DD'si (11,5) 31 Ocak 2026 bilançosuna dayanıyordu; şirketin 31 Temmuz 2026 bilançosuyla (özsermaye 364,0 milyon sterlin, 196,9 milyon pay; investing.com'da hisse başına defter değeri 1,85 sterlin) 9,16 olarak düzeltildi.

Goodwin'de F/K (175,6) yalnız süren faaliyetlerin kârına dayanır; kaynak, ikinci kaynak ve investing.com aynı esası kullanıyor. Şirketin 30 Nisan 2026'da biten yılda açıkladığı toplam hisse başına kârla (738,44 peni; satılmak üzere ayrılan makine mühendisliği bölümü dahil) F/K yaklaşık 19,8 olur. Bölümün satışı anlaşıldı, henüz tamamlanmadı.

Rio Tinto'da kaynağın piyasa değeri (109,6 milyar sterlin) çift kotasyonlu grubun tamamını kapsar; yalnız Londra'da işlem gören Rio Tinto plc paylarının değeri yaklaşık 79,4 milyar sterlindir (1.255 milyon pay, şirketin 30 Eylül 2026 bildirimi). F/K ve PD/DD hisse başına hesaplandığı için bundan etkilenmez. HSBC, AstraZeneca, Shell ve Rolls-Royce'ta fiyat, piyasa değeri, F/K ve PD/DD ikinci kaynakla %4 içinde tutuyor.

Kaynağın PD/DD alanı boş olan 82 şirkette PD/DD aynı kaynağın son bilanço alanlarından hesaplandı (26 şirkette son açıklanan, 56 şirkette son yıllık bilanço); hangisi olduğu şirketin sayfasında yazar. Denetim: Avon Technologies'te kaynak 5,00, şirketin 30 Eylül 2026 bilançosuyla hesap yaklaşık 4,8.

Veri kaynağı 128 şirkette son 12 ayın kârını vermiyor. En büyükleri: Airtel Mobile Commerce, Rosebank Industries, IG Group, Canal+, Princes Group ve Applied Nutrition. Bu şirketler zararda değil; kaynakta kâr verisi olmadığı için değerlendirilemedi ve sayfalarında 'kâr verisi eksik' yazar.

Beş yıllık oranlar: stockanalysis.com oran sayfaları. 47 adayın sayfası bulunamadı (Rolls-Royce, BAE Systems, United Utilities, JD Sports ve Jet2 dahil): kodu noktayla biten paylar ve AIM payları başka adreste duruyor. Adres kalıbı 13 Kasım 2026'da düzeltildi; bu şirketler veri gelene kadar 2. surda 'veri eksik' olarak durur.

İngiliz şirketlerinin çoğu yılda iki kez bilanço açıklar; mali yıl her şirkette takvim yılıyla bitmez. Grafikte şirketin kendi mali yılları yazar; enflasyon düzeltmesi aynı adı taşıyan takvim yılının oranıyla yapılır. Dolar ya da avroyla raporlayan şirketlerde de düzeltme Birleşik Krallık enflasyonuyla yapıldı.

Yıl sonu enflasyonu: Ulusal İstatistik Ofisi (ONS), tüketici fiyat endeksi (D7G7 serisi), aralık ayı yıllık oranları (2021-2025). Son yıllık oran: ONS, Eylül 2026 (%3,5); ekim oranı 18 Kasım 2026'da açıklanacak.
3. sur okuması sırayla yapılır: önce fiyatı kale olmaya yetenler. Okunmayan şirket 'sırada' görünür.

en.inflation_note: UK companies do not apply inflation accounting. The return on equity of every company was therefore adjusted by year-end consumer inflation: 5.4% for 2021, 10.5% for 2022, 4.0% for 2023, 2.5% for 2024 and 3.4% for 2025. For the last 12 months the most recently published annual rate (September 2026, 3.5%) was used.
data_notes: Price, market value, P/E and P/B: TradingView screener, 12 November 2026. Prices are in pence (GBX), market values in millions of pounds. The universe is 1,071 stocks: 1,034 on the London Stock Exchange (Main Market and AIM) and 37 on the Aquis Stock Exchange. Depositary receipts, stocks whose main listing is in another country and most closed-end funds are not in the universe; the 30 investment trusts that are in it stay outside at Wall 1.

For comparison: the London Stock Exchange's own current list could not be opened in this run. According to secondary sources there were 1,534 companies on the London Stock Exchange in May 2026, funds included (Fortune, citing exchange data). According to the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), 512 commercial companies had shares listed on the Main Market in June 2026; AIM had 619 companies at the end of 2025. For non-fund companies the universe is about 11% below that total (about 1,130). Aquis has about 80 companies; 37 of them are in the universe.

Corrected with a third source (13 November 2026). IG Design Group: the source showed a P/E of 26.3; in the company's results for the year ended 31 March 2026 the result attributable to the parent is a loss of 112.3 million pounds (continuing operations a profit of 5.4 million, discontinued operations a loss of 117.7 million). The company was marked as loss-making. Softcat: the source's P/B (11.5) rested on the balance sheet of 31 January 2026; with the company's balance sheet of 31 July 2026 (equity 364.0 million pounds, 196.9 million shares; book value per share of 1.85 pounds on investing.com) it was corrected to 9.16.

For Goodwin the P/E (175.6) rests on profit from continuing operations only; the source, the second source and investing.com all use that basis. With the total earnings per share the company reported for the year ended 30 April 2026 (738.44 pence, including the mechanical engineering division held for sale) the P/E is about 19.8. The sale of the division has been agreed but is not yet complete.

For Rio Tinto the source's market value (109.6 billion pounds) covers the whole dual-listed group; the Rio Tinto plc shares traded in London alone are worth about 79.4 billion pounds (1,255 million shares, company notice as at 30 September 2026). P/E and P/B are calculated per share and are not affected. For HSBC, AstraZeneca, Shell and Rolls-Royce, price, market value, P/E and P/B agree with the second source within 4%.

For 82 companies where the source's P/B field is empty, P/B was calculated from the same source's latest balance-sheet fields (the latest reported balance sheet for 26 companies, the last annual balance sheet for 56); the company's page says which. Check: for Avon Technologies the source gives 5.00; with the company's balance sheet of 30 September 2026 the figure is about 4.8.

For 128 companies the data source gives no profit figure for the last 12 months. The largest are Airtel Mobile Commerce, Rosebank Industries, IG Group, Canal+, Princes Group and Applied Nutrition. These companies are not loss-making; they could not be assessed because the source has no profit data, and their pages say 'profit data missing'.

Five-year ratios: stockanalysis.com ratio pages. The pages of 47 candidates could not be found (including Rolls-Royce, BAE Systems, United Utilities, JD Sports and Jet2): stocks whose ticker ends in a dot and AIM stocks sit at a different address. The address pattern was corrected on 13 November 2026; until the data arrives these companies stay at Wall 2 as 'data missing'.

Most UK companies publish a balance sheet twice a year, and the fiscal year does not end with the calendar year for every company. The chart shows each company's own fiscal years; the inflation adjustment uses the rate of the calendar year with the same name. For companies that report in dollars or euros the adjustment was also made with UK inflation.

Year-end inflation: Office for National Statistics (ONS), consumer prices index (series D7G7), December annual rates (2021-2025). Latest annual rate: ONS, September 2026 (3.5%); the October rate is due on 18 November 2026.
The Wall 3 reading is done in order: companies priced low enough to be castles come first. A company that has not been read yet is shown as 'in the queue'.
en.small_rule: Companies with a market value below 50 million pounds (about 66 million US dollars) are left out.

ALTN.one: Kazakistan'da tek madenden altın çıkaran şirket. Kalite surlarını geçti; kârı altın fiyatı belirlediği için hendek surunda elendi.
ALTN.business: AltynGold, Kazakistan'ın doğusundaki Sekisovskoye yeraltı madeninden altın çıkarır ve satar. Geliri satılan ons ile altın fiyatının çarpımıdır. 2026'nın ilk yarısında 24.628 ons altın sattı; ortalama satış fiyatı ons başına 4.615 dolar, hasılat 115,2 milyon dolar oldu. Şirket dolarla raporlar; hisseleri Londra'da işlem görür.
ALTN.moat_text: Hendek yok. Altın bir emtiadır; şirket fiyatı kendisi belirleyemez. İlk yarıda hasılat %64,6 arttı, ama satılan ons yalnız %9,0 arttı; artışın kalanı altın fiyatındaki %50,3'lük yükselişten geldi. Reel özsermaye kârlılığı da fiyatı izliyor: 2022'de %10,9, 2023'te %12,6, 2025'te %48,4. Maliyet üstünlüğü de kanıtlı değil: toplam sürdürme maliyeti ons başına 1.299 dolardan 1.995 dolara çıktı. Şirket tek madene bağlı; madenin lisansı 2029'a kadar. B puanı 0 olduğu için şirket bu surda elendi.
ALTN.mgmt: Şirketi Assaubayev ailesi yönetir: başkan, genel müdür ve bir icra kurulu üyesi aileden. Bir veri sitesine göre hisselerin %65,6'sı ailenin şirketi AGold Mining Group'ta; şirketin kendi belgesinden doğrulayamadık. Temettü ödenmiyor, geri alım yok; yönetim kurulu bir temettü politikasını inceliyor. Kâr madene ve borca gidiyor: ilk yarıda 26,1 milyon dolar yatırım yapıldı, borç 41,2 milyon dolardan 31,4 milyon dolara indi. 2026-2028 için 95 milyon dolarlık yatırım planı var. Aileye bağlı şirketlerle işlemler var; Altyn Group Qazaqstan'dan 2,8 milyon dolar alacak duruyor.
ALTN.latest: 29 Eylül 2026: Ocak-Haziran 2026 hasılatı 115,2 milyon dolar (geçen yıl 70,0 milyon; +%64,6). Net kâr 42,7 milyon dolar (27,0 milyon; +%58,4), hisse başına kâr 156,38 sent (98,71 sent). Satış maliyeti 29,8 milyon dolardan 55,3 milyon dolara çıktı; toplam sürdürme maliyeti ons başına 1.995 dolar (1.299 dolar). Net borç 19,3 milyon dolar. Şirket 2026 için 52-55 bin onsluk üretim hedefini korudu. 25 Ağustos 2026'da Teren-Sai sahasının sözleşmesinin uzatılması onaylandı.
risks: Kâr altın fiyatına bağlı: ilk yarıdaki ortalama satış fiyatı ons başına 4.615 dolardı, 2025'te 3.474 dolar. Fiyat düşerse kâr hızla düşer; satılan ons yılda yalnız %9 arttı.
Tek maden, tek ülke: bütün üretim Sekisovskoye'den gelir ve madenin lisansı 2029'a kadar. Uzatma Kazakistan devletinin kararına bağlı.
Maliyet hızla artıyor: toplam sürdürme maliyeti bir yılda ons başına 1.299 dolardan 1.995 dolara çıktı. Şirket artışın yarısından fazlasını altının değeriyle artan maden çıkarma vergisine bağlıyor.
Şirket Kazakistan'da çalışır ve dolarla raporlar; sayfadaki enflasyon düzeltmesi Birleşik Krallık enflasyonuyla yapıldı. Aile şirketi çoğunluğa sahip, halka açık pay küçük ve temettü yok.

en.one: A gold miner with a single mine in Kazakhstan. It passed the quality walls; it was eliminated at the moat wall because the gold price sets its profit.
en.business: AltynGold mines and sells gold from the Sekisovskoye underground mine in eastern Kazakhstan. Its revenue is ounces sold times the gold price. In the first half of 2026 it sold 24,628 ounces at an average price of 4,615 dollars an ounce, for revenue of 115.2 million dollars. The company reports in dollars; its shares trade in London.
en.moat_text: There is no moat. Gold is a commodity; the company cannot set its own price. First-half revenue rose 64.6%, but ounces sold rose only 9.0%; the rest came from a 50.3% rise in the gold price. Real return on equity follows the price too: 10.9% in 2022, 12.6% in 2023, 48.4% in 2025. A cost advantage is not proven either: all-in sustaining cost rose from 1,299 to 1,995 dollars an ounce. The company depends on one mine, whose licence runs to 2029. With a B score of 0 the company was eliminated at this wall.
en.mgmt: The Assaubayev family runs the company: the chairman, the chief executive and one executive director are family members. According to a data site, 65.6% of the shares are held by the family's company AGold Mining Group; we could not confirm this from the company's own document. No dividend is paid and there are no buybacks; the board is reviewing a dividend policy. Profit goes into the mine and to debt: 26.1 million dollars was invested in the first half, and borrowings fell from 41.2 million to 31.4 million dollars. An investment plan of 95 million dollars covers 2026-2028. There are dealings with family-related companies; 2.8 million dollars is still owed by Altyn Group Qazaqstan.
en.latest: 29 September 2026: Revenue for January-June 2026 was 115.2 million dollars (70.0 million a year earlier; +64.6%). Net profit was 42.7 million dollars (27.0 million; +58.4%) and earnings per share 156.38 cents (98.71 cents). Cost of sales rose from 29.8 million to 55.3 million dollars; all-in sustaining cost was 1,995 dollars an ounce (1,299 dollars). Net debt was 19.3 million dollars. The company kept its 2026 production target of 52-55 thousand ounces. On 25 August 2026 the extension of the contract for the Teren-Sai site was approved.
risks: Profit depends on the gold price: the average selling price in the first half was 4,615 dollars an ounce, against 3,474 dollars in 2025. If the price falls, profit falls fast; ounces sold rose only 9% in a year.
One mine, one country: all production comes from Sekisovskoye, and the mine's licence runs to 2029. An extension depends on a decision by the state of Kazakhstan.

Costs are rising fast: all-in sustaining cost went from 1,299 to 1,995 dollars an ounce in a year. The company puts more than half of the increase down to the mineral extraction tax, which rises with the value of gold.

The company operates in Kazakhstan and reports in dollars; the inflation adjustment on the page was made with United Kingdom inflation. A family company holds the majority, the free float is small and there is no dividend.

BGEO.one: Gürcistan ve Ermenistan'ın en büyük kredi veren bankalarının sahibi. Kalite surlarını geçti; marj, kârın ve yılda %15,4 reel büyümenin süreceği varsayımına dayanıyor.
BGEO.business: Lion Finance Group (eski adıyla Bank of Georgia Group), Gürcistan'da Bank of Georgia'nın, Ermenistan'da Ameriabank'ın sahibidir. Parayı kredi faizi ile mevduat faizi arasındaki farktan ve ödeme, kart komisyonlarından kazanır. 30 Eylül 2026'da 46,5 milyar lari kredisi ve 44,9 milyar lari mevduatı vardı. 2026'nın ilk dokuz ayında kârın 1.419 milyon larisi Gürcistan'dan, 434 milyon larisi Ermenistan'dan geldi. Şirket Londra'da işlem görür ama hesaplarını lari ile tutar.
BGEO.moat_text: Hendek dar. Üstünlük ölçekten ve müşterinin günlük bankası olmaktan geliyor. Şirketin yatırımcı sunumunun özetine göre Bank of Georgia, Mart 2026'da Gürcistan'da kredilerin %38'iyle birinciydi; ülkenin iki büyük bankası sektör varlıklarının %76,6'sını tutuyor (2025'in ilk sekiz ayı). Ameriabank Ermenistan'da kredilerin %23,0'üyle birinci. Bank of Georgia'nın üye işyeri ödeme hacmindeki payı %56,8; aylık 2,35 milyon etkin bireysel müşterisi var. Bu, rakamlarda görünüyor: net faiz marjı %6,5, gider/gelir oranı %32,1, reel özsermaye kârlılığı beş yılın ortalamasında %26, en düşük yılında %19. 2024'ün %38'lik okuması Ameriabank alımından doğan tek seferlik kazançla şişmiştir. Zayıf yanı: üstünlük iki küçük ülkeyle sınırlı ve o ülkelerin merkez bankası kurallarına, siyasetine, kuruna bağlı. Bu yüzden geniş değil, dar.
BGEO.mgmt: Şirketi profesyonel yönetim yürütüyor. Bilinen en büyük ortak Georgia Capital'dir: Ağustos 2025 bildirimine göre oyların %18,12'si; daha yeni bir bildirim okunamadı. Kâr üçe bölünüyor: büyüyen kredilere sermaye, çeyreklik temettü ve geri alınıp iptal edilen hisseler. 2025'te hisse başına 10,50 lari temettü ve 203 milyon larilik geri alımla dağıtım oranı %30 oldu; hedef %30-50. 2026'da çeyreklik temettü 2,85, 3,05 ve 3,25 lariye çıktı; dört ayrı geri alım programı açıklandı (53,5, 55, 59 ve 62 milyon lari). Ameriabank 2024'te yaklaşık 303,6 milyon dolara alındı ve bugün kârın dörtte birine yakınını getiriyor. Şirketin merkezi Tiflis'te, tescili Londra'da. Üst yönetimin ücreti yüksek: 30 kişilik kilit yöneticilere 2025'in ilk yarısında 79,1 milyon lari ödendi, bunun 39,7 milyon larisi hisse olarak. Şirketin 'tek seferlik kalemler hariç' kârı yalnız 29,6 milyon larilik bir defalık hisse ödeme düzeltmesini dışarıda bırakıyor; olağan hisse ödemeleri kârdan düşülmüş durumda.
BGEO.latest: 3 Kasım 2026: Şirket üçüncü çeyrekte 661,9 milyon lari kâr açıkladı (geçen yıl 547,2 milyon; +%21,0). Seyreltilmiş hisse başına kâr 15,42 lari (geçen yıl 12,58). Dokuz aylık kâr 1.865,7 milyon lari (geçen yıl ana ortaklık payı 1.571,6 milyon), hisse başına 43,38 lari (geçen yıl 35,99). Krediler sabit kurla yılda %24,6 büyüdü: Gürcistan %18,6, Ermenistan %38,1. Özsermaye kârlılığı (şirketin açıkladığı) %27,2, risk maliyeti %0,7, sorunlu kredi oranı %2,0. Ana ortaklığa ait özsermaye 9.910,5 milyon lari. Çeyrek temettüsü hisse başına 3,25 lari; geri alım programı 62 milyon lari uzatıldı. Sonuç metninde kârı şişiren tek seferlik bir kazanç yok.
risks: Hesap yılda %15,4 reel büyüme varsayıyor. Marj büyüme varsayımına ve bugünkü kârın sürmesine dayanıyor. Şirketin kendi orta vade hedefi yılda yaklaşık %15 kredi büyümesi ve en az %20 özsermaye kârlılığı; bugünkü rakamlar (%24,6 ve %27,2) bunların üstünde. Büyüme ve kârlılık hedefe doğru inerse marj daralır.

Sermaye tamponları ince: 30 Eylül 2026'da Bank of Georgia'nın toplam sermaye oranı alt sınırın 2,0 puan, Ameriabank'ınki 1,5 puan üstünde. Lari %10 değer kaybederse Bank of Georgia'nın çekirdek sermaye oranı yaklaşık 0,8 puan düşer; bu, büyümeyi ve dağıtımı sınırlayabilir.

Şirket Birleşik Krallık'ta değil, Gürcistan ve Ermenistan'da çalışıyor ve lari ile raporluyor. Enflasyon düzeltmesi Birleşik Krallık enflasyonuyla yapıldı; lari ya da dram değer kaybederse sterlin cinsinden kâr düşer.
Siyaset ve bölge riski: şirket, Ekim 2024 seçimlerinden sonraki siyasi gerginliği ve Rusya'ya yakınlıktan doğan yaptırım riskini kendi risk listesinde sayıyor.
Kredilerin ve mevduatın yaklaşık %40'ı yabancı para. Kur sert oynarsa borçlunun ödeme gücü bozulur; risk maliyeti bugün çok düşük (%0,7) ve buradan yükselebilir.

en.one: Owner of the largest lenders in Georgia and Armenia. Passed the quality walls; the margin rests on profit holding up and assumed real growth of 15.4% a year.
en.business: Lion Finance Group (formerly Bank of Georgia Group) owns Bank of Georgia in Georgia and Ameriabank in Armenia. It earns the spread between loan interest and deposit interest, plus payment and card fees. At 30 September 2026 it had 46.5 billion lari of loans and 44.9 billion lari of deposits. In the first nine months of 2026, 1,419 million lari of profit came from Georgia and 434 million lari from Armenia. The company is listed in London but keeps its accounts in lari.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The advantage comes from scale and from being the customer's everyday bank. According to a summary of the company's investor presentation, Bank of Georgia was first in Georgia with 38% of loans in March 2026; the country's two large banks hold 76.6% of sector assets (first eight months of 2025). Ameriabank is first in Armenia with 23.0% of loans. Bank of Georgia's share of merchant acquiring volume is 56.8%; it has 2.35 million monthly active retail customers. This shows in the numbers: net interest margin 6.5%, cost-to-income ratio 32.1%, real return on equity averaging 26% over five years and 19% in its lowest year. The 38% reading for 2024 is inflated by a one-off gain from the Ameriabank purchase. The weak point: the advantage is confined to two small countries and depends on their central bank rules, politics and currencies. That is why it is narrow, not wide.
en.mgmt: The company is run by professional management. The largest known shareholder is Georgia Capital: 18.12% of the votes according to an August 2025 notification; no newer notification could be read. Profit is split three ways: capital for the growing loan book, a quarterly dividend, and shares bought back and cancelled. In 2025 a dividend of 10.50 lari a share and 203 million lari of buybacks gave a payout ratio of 30%; the target is 30-50%. In 2026 the quarterly dividend rose to 2.85, 3.05 and 3.25 lari; four separate buyback programmes were announced (53.5, 55, 59 and 62 million lari). Ameriabank was bought in 2024 for about 303.6 million dollars and now brings in close to a quarter of profit. The head office is in Tbilisi and the company is registered in London. Senior pay is high: the 30 key managers received GEL 79.1 million in the first half of 2025, of which GEL 39.7 million in shares. The company's profit 'adjusted for one-offs' excludes only a GEL 29.6 million one-time share-award catch-up; ordinary share-based pay is already deducted from profit.
en.latest: 3 November 2026: The company reported third-quarter profit of 661.9 million lari (547.2 million a year earlier; +21.0%). Diluted earnings per share were 15.42 lari (12.58 a year earlier). Nine-month profit was 1,865.7 million lari (1,571.6 million attributable to shareholders a year earlier), or 43.38 lari a share (35.99 a year earlier). Loans grew 24.6% year on year in constant currency: Georgia 18.6%, Armenia 38.1%. Return on equity (as reported by the company) was 27.2%, cost of risk 0.7%, the non-performing loan ratio 2.0%. Equity attributable to shareholders was 9,910.5 million lari. The quarterly dividend is 3.25 lari a share; the buyback programme was extended by 62 million lari. The results text shows no one-off gain inflating profit.
risks: The calculation assumes real growth of 15.4% a year. The margin rests on the growth assumption and on today's profit holding up. The company's own medium-term targets are loan growth of about 15% a year and return on equity of at least 20%; today's figures (24.6% and 27.2%) are above them. If growth and profitability come down towards the targets, the margin narrows.

Capital buffers are thin: on 30 September 2026 Bank of Georgia's total capital ratio was 2.0 points above its minimum and Ameriabank's 1.5 points. A 10% fall in the lari cuts Bank of Georgia's CET1 ratio by about 0.8 points; this can limit growth and payouts.
The company operates in Georgia and Armenia, not in the UK, and reports in lari. The inflation adjustment was made with UK inflation; if the lari or the dram loses value, profit in sterling falls.
Political and regional risk: the company lists the political tension after the October 2024 elections and the sanctions risk from proximity to Russia among its own risks.
About 40% of loans and deposits are in foreign currency. A sharp currency move weakens borrowers' ability to pay; cost of risk is very low today (0.7%) and can rise from here.

en.one: North America's largest seller of promotional products. It passed the quality walls, but profit is falling in 2026 and company guidance is below last year.
en.business: 4imprint sells promotional products printed with a logo to businesses and organisations: pens, bags, T-shirts, mugs. It finds customers through catalogues, the internet and television advertising; the supplier prints the order and ships it straight to the customer, so the company holds no stock. In 2025 revenue was 1,346.8 million dollars on 2.06 million orders. In the first half of 2026, 98% of revenue came from North America. The company is listed in London but reports in dollars.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The advantage comes from scale, a well-known brand and a business model that needs little capital. By its own estimate the company is the largest seller in a fragmented US and Canadian market of 27.7 billion dollars; its share is about 5% (our calculation). Real return on equity averaged 57% over five years and was 24% in its lowest year. The return on average capital employed reported by the company was 87% in 2025. About 80% of orders come from existing customers; each dollar spent on marketing brought in 7.86 dollars of revenue. The weak point: the product is ordinary and switching to a competitor is easy. The share of customers who reorder within 24 months is 45%. Orders from new customers fell 12% in 2025. Tariffs cut the gross margin from 32.8% to 31.5% in the first half of 2026; price increases did not fully make up for it.
en.mgmt: The company has no controlling shareholder; the largest holder is BlackRock (7.13%, February 2026). There is no debt; cash was 136.9 million dollars at 27 June 2026. Profit goes first to the business, then to dividends: in 2025 it paid a regular dividend of 240 cents per share and a special dividend of 250 cents (142.8 million dollars in total). The company makes no acquisitions; it hands out surplus cash through special dividends. Buybacks are negligible: 5.4 million dollars of shares were bought in 2025 for employee share plans. The financial year ends on the Saturday at the end of December; the company reports results twice a year, with trading updates in between.
en.latest: 10 November 2026: The company published its trading update for the first ten months. Revenue was 2% above last year, order count 1% below, and average order value 3% higher. Orders from new customers fell 5% (first quarter −9%, second −5%, third −3%). The operating margin was just above 9%. Cash was 152 million dollars at the end of October. The 2026 outlook was kept: revenue slightly above 2025 (1.35 billion dollars) and adjusted profit before tax of about 130 million dollars (2025: 150.8 million). First-half results announced on 5 August 2026: revenue 666.4 million dollars (+1%), net profit 43.5 million dollars (55.5 million a year earlier), earnings per share 155.1 cents (197.4). Profit includes a one-off charge of 5.1 million dollars for uncertain tax treatments.
risks: Profit is falling: earnings per share dropped 21% in the first half of 2026 (12% excluding the one-off charge). The company's 2026 outlook for adjusted profit before tax is about 130 million dollars; it was 150.8 million in 2025. If the price calculation rests on past growth, the margin of safety looks higher than it is.
Tariffs are raising supplier costs. The gross margin fell from 32.8% to 31.5% in the first half; if tariff policy changes again, the margin may narrow further.
New customer acquisition is weak: orders from new customers fell 12% in 2025 and 5% in the first ten months of 2026. Growth depends on how well marketing works.
Promotional products are bought out of companies' marketing budgets; they are among the first expenses cut when the economy slows. In 2021 real return on equity fell to 24%.

The company works almost entirely in the US and reports in dollars; the inflation adjustment here was made with UK inflation. Because the share trades in sterling, the exchange rate also affects the price.

en.one: Runs photobooths and self-service laundry machines. Passed the quality walls; the margin assumes real growth of 5.1% a year, yet the company cut its 2026 profit outlook.
en.business: ME Group runs about 49,700 vending units in 16 countries: 30,356 photobooths (Photo.ME) and 8,106 outdoor laundry machines in supermarket car parks (Wash.ME). It earns the fee the customer pays into the machine and gives the site owner a share. In the fiscal year ended 31 October 2025 revenue was 315.4 million pounds and profit before tax 78.2 million pounds. Continental Europe brings 68.3% of revenue and 80.1% of EBITDA; France is the largest and most profitable market.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The advantage comes from scale and site contracts: more than 30 thousand booths and multi-year agreements with stations and supermarkets (SNCF renewed for five years, RATP for seven). The proof in numbers: real return on equity averaged 22.6% over five years and is 23.8% for the last 12 months; fiscal 2025 EBITDA was 120.4 million pounds, 38% of revenue. The laundry arm is growing: revenue of 112.4 million pounds in 2025 (+17.3%), 46.1% of group EBITDA. The weak side: photobooth revenue is falling (−4.0% in 2025, −6.2% in the first half of 2026). ID photo rules are in the hands of governments; a rule change in Germany cut demand. In laundry the advantage depends on the site; its durability is less proven than in booths.
en.mgmt: A founder-family company: chief executive Serge Crasnianski holds 36.49% of the votes (23 March 2026). More than half of profit goes to dividends: 8.64 pence a share for 2025, 58% of profit. A buyback of up to 18 million pounds began in March 2026; 4.5 million pounds of shares had been bought by July. The rest goes into new laundry machines (capital spending of 65.6 million pounds in 2025). Flaws: the company put itself up for sale in June 2025 and ended the process in December 2025, saying no adequate offer had come. The audit of the 2025 accounts was delayed and the shares were temporarily suspended in March 2026; past balance sheets were restated for an error in counting the cash inside the machines (cash down 8.7 million pounds; profit unchanged). The fiscal year ends in October. The GBP 2.28 million paid to directors includes amounts paid to companies they control for their services; no separate figure is given. Acquisitions are small and in the core business: two Belgian photobooth operators, paid in cash.
en.latest: 13 July 2026: In the six months ended 30 April 2026 revenue was 154.3 million pounds (+0.3%), profit before tax 32.7 million pounds (−3.8%), net profit 24.5 million pounds (25.6 million a year earlier) and diluted earnings per share 6.48 pence (6.74). Photobooth revenue fell 6.2%; laundry revenue rose 16.3%. The interim dividend was cut from 3.85 pence to 3.60 pence. Net cash was 7.5 million pounds (27.6 million a year earlier). On 1 June 2026 the company had set its full-year profit before tax outlook at 69–74 million pounds (2025: 78.2 million); the shares fell 26% that day. The reason: in April booth revenue fell 17%, especially in France. In May vending revenue rose 11.1%; the company repeated the outlook.
risks: The calculation assumes real growth of 5.1% a year. The price calculation rests on the last 12 months' profit and on the growth assumption; both are weakening. The company's 2026 profit before tax outlook is 69–74 million pounds against 78.2 million last year; earnings per share fell 3.9% in the first half. The fiscal year ended on 31 October 2026 and the results are not out yet.
The company has provided for tax reassessments in France, which lifted the effective tax rate from 26.3% to 27.7%; it does not disclose the amount.

Photobooth revenue may be in structural decline: −4.0% in 2025 and −6.2% in the first half of 2026. If governments move ID photos to digital channels (as with the rule change in Germany), fewer booths are needed.

Most of the business is outside the UK: 68.3% of revenue comes from Continental Europe, mostly France; there is Japan too. The inflation adjustment was made with UK inflation; profit also depends on the euro and the yen.

Accounting and governance questions: the 2025 audit was delayed, the cash figure was restated for past years, and a provision was made for tax reassessments in France. One person holds 36.49% of the votes.

en.one: A gold producer in South Africa and Australia. It passed the quality walls, but its profit follows the gold price; no moat, so it failed Wall 3.
en.business: Pan African Resources mines and sells gold. Its mines are in South Africa (Barberton, Evander, and the tailings retreatment plants Elikhulu and MTR) and in Australia (Tennant Creek). In the fiscal year ended June 2026 it produced 272,310 ounces of gold; revenue was 1,156.5 million dollars and profit attributable to owners 357.2 million dollars. The company reports in US dollars; its fiscal year ends in June.
en.moat_text: There is no moat. Gold is a commodity; the company does not set its price. The jump in profit came from the price: the average price received rose from 2,735 to 4,235 dollars an ounce (+54.8%), and revenue rose 114.2%. In the same year the all-in sustaining cost rose from 1,600 to 1,867 dollars an ounce; the company expects 2,075–2,175 dollars for fiscal 2027. Real return on equity rose from 14% to 40.2% over five years (average 26.3%); that is the trace of the gold price, not of a lasting advantage. The strong point: part of production comes from low-cost tailings retreatment (1,231 dollars an ounce at Elikhulu). At Barberton the cost is 2,430 dollars. This filter does not count a commodity producer as having a moat; the company fails Wall 3 for that reason.
en.mgmt: Profit went to debt, dividends and new mines. Net debt of 150.5 million dollars turned into net cash of 185.7 million dollars in one year. The dividend for the year is 77 South African cents a share (3.53 pence; 37 cents a year earlier). The company announced a share buyback of up to 500 million rand starting in October 2026. Capital expenditure was 224.0 million dollars; 330 million dollars is planned for fiscal 2027. A small flaw: Emmerson Resources in Australia was bought with 102.6 million new shares issued on 1 July 2026 (148.2 million dollars); this raised the shares outstanding by about 5%. Of the issued shares, 306.4 million are held by PAR Gold, a group company. Allan Gray reported 5.06% of the voting rights on 20 August 2026. The primary listing is in Johannesburg (JSE); the share also trades in London and, since June 2026, in Australia.
en.latest: 16 September 2026: Audited results for the fiscal year ended June 2026 were published. Revenue was 1,156.5 million dollars (+114.2%), profit attributable to owners 357.2 million dollars (141.6 million a year earlier), earnings per share 17.60 US cents (7.16 a year earlier). Production was 272,310 ounces (+38.6%) at an all-in sustaining cost of 1,867 dollars an ounce. Net cash was 185.7 million dollars. The final dividend is 65 South African cents a share; it goes to a vote at the annual general meeting on 19 November 2026. Outlook for fiscal 2027: production of 280,000–302,000 ounces at a cost of 2,075–2,175 dollars an ounce.

en.one: One of Georgia's two largest banks, with a digital bank in Uzbekistan. Passed the quality walls; the margin rests on assumed real growth of 11.2% a year; Uzbek profit is falling.
en.business: TBC Bank Group lends to individuals and companies and takes deposits in Georgia; it also offers leasing, insurance and payment services. In Uzbekistan it runs a retail bank that works only by phone. It earns the spread between loan interest and funding cost, plus fees. At 30 September 2026 it had 32.5 billion lari of loans and 27.6 billion lari of customer deposits; in the first nine months of 2026 about 99% of profit came from Georgia. The company is listed in London but keeps its accounts in lari.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. Georgian banking is in the hands of two large banks; TBC's share of loans and deposits is about 37-40%, and 43.6% in corporate loans (31 December 2025, central bank data). This scale shows in the margins: net interest margin 7.4%, cost-to-income ratio 38.7%. Real return on equity averaged 19.2% over five years and was 15.0% in the lowest year. The weak side: the advantage depends on one small country and on that country's banking rules. In Uzbekistan the share is small (about 4.2% of retail loans) and new rules have cut profit; there is no evidence for a wide moat.
en.mgmt: The company's dividend policy is to pay out at least 25% of profit. For 2025 it paid a dividend of 8.87 lari a share (35% of profit); with a 75 million lari buyback the payout was 40% of profit. In 2026 it declared 1.75 lari each quarter; on 6 November 2026 it announced a new 50 million lari buyback. The rest of the profit goes into loan growth and Uzbekistan. The company owns 79.7% of the Uzbek business; EBRD and IFC hold the rest (10.15% each). Uzbekistan earned 127 million lari in 2025; the company's own target was 200 million lari. No current shareholder table showing a controlling owner could be read in this run; Allan Gray reported that its holding fell to 2.98% (18 September 2026). Bought-back shares are cancelled: 436,797 in 2024 and 465,746 in 2025; the share count is down 1.0% since end-2024. Share-based pay cost GEL 40.2 million in 2025, 2.8% of profit; the company reports profit after deducting it.
en.latest: 6 November 2026: The company reported third-quarter net profit attributable to shareholders of 400.7 million lari (+11.5%); diluted earnings per share were 7.19 lari (+12.2%). Nine-month profit was 1,142.5 million lari (+12.3%). Return on equity as reported by the company was 23.2% (24.4% a year earlier). The Georgian arm earned 406.2 million lari (+17.4%); Uzbekistan earned 15.9 million lari (−61.2%), with a cost of risk of 10.8% there. Loans grew 16% at constant currency. The non-performing loan ratio was 3.3% (2.7% a year earlier). The quarterly dividend is 1.75 lari.
risks: The calculation assumes real growth of 11.2% a year. The price calculation rests on the last 12 months' profit holding up and on growth continuing. Uzbekistan's profit fell 39.7% in nine months; if credit losses or margins worsen in Georgia, the margin of safety shrinks. No one-off gain was found in the last 12 months' profit.
The non-performing loan ratio has risen for three years: 2.0% at end-2023, 2.7% at end-2025 and 3.3% in September 2026. Provision coverage fell from 79.8% to 67.2% over the same period.

The company operates in Georgia and Uzbekistan, not in the United Kingdom, and reports in lari. The inflation adjustment was made with UK inflation; if the lari loses value against sterling, profit in sterling falls.
Almost all profit comes from one small country. The company's own risk list starts with internal political tension in Georgia and Uzbekistan and with the wars in the region.
50.6% of loans are in foreign currency (31 December 2025). A sharp fall in the lari would weaken borrowers' ability to pay and the capital ratios.

SNWS.business: Smiths News, gazete ve dergileri yayıncılardan alır ve her sabah İngiltere ve Galler'de 21.000'den fazla satış noktasına dağıtır. Parayı dağıtım payından kazanır; her bölgede yayıncının tek toptancısıdır. 29 Ağustos 2026'da biten mali yılda hasılat 1.036,2 milyon sterlin, düzeltilmiş faaliyet kârı 38,7 milyon sterlin oldu. Koleksiyon kartları ve atık kâğıt geri dönüşümü gibi yan işler büyüyor, ama küçük.
SNWS.moat_text: Hendek dar. Üstünlük, yayıncılarla yapılan uzun süreli ve bölgede tek yetkili sözleşmelerden ve her sabah çalışan dağıtım ağının ölçeğinden geliyor. Şirket 2026'da News UK, Telegraph, Associated Newspapers, Frontline ve Seymour ile sözleşmelerini 2036-2037'ye uzattı ve yeni bölgeler aldı; yeni sözleşmeler başladığında ülke gazete ve dergi pazarının yaklaşık %61'i onda olacak. Düzeltilmiş faaliyet kârı iki yıldır aynı düzeyde (38,7 ve 39,1 milyon sterlin). Zayıf yanı: basılı gazete pazarı yapısal olarak küçülüyor; gazete geliri 2026'da %4,1, dergi geliri %3,2 düştü ve şirketin kendi uzun vadeli varsayımı yılda %3-5 düşüş. Kâr marjı ince (hasılatın yaklaşık %3,7'si) ve birkaç büyük yayıncıya bağlı. Özsermaye çok küçük (10,7 milyon sterlin) olduğu için grafikteki reel özsermaye kârlılığı rakamları (2025'te %880, 2026'da %230) işin kalitesini ölçmüyor; önceki yıllarda özsermaye eksiydi.
SNWS.mgmt: Hisseler halka yaygın; hâkim ortak yok. Aberforth Partners'ın payı 28 Ekim 2026'da %14,8'e indi. Kâr borç ödemeye ve temettüye gitti: şirket Ağustos 2025'te ilk kez net nakde geçti (banka net nakdi 2026 sonunda 3,9 milyon sterlin). 2026 için hisse başına 5,65 peni olağan temettü önerildi (2025: 5,55 peni artı 3,00 peni özel temettü); bu yıl özel temettü yok. Yıl içinde 20,9 milyon sterlin temettü ödendi; çalışan pay planları için 5,3 milyon sterlinlik hisse alındı. Hisse geri alım programı yok. Şimdi para ana işe gidiyor: ülke çapına yayılma programının maliyeti 21-27 milyon sterlin. Geçmişten kalan bir sorun var: Emeklilik Düzenleyicisi, satılmış olan Tuffnells'in emeklilik planı için şirkete mali destek talimatı vermeyi değerlendiriyor (tahmini yükümlülük 3,3 milyon sterlin; karşılık ayrılmadı). Mali yıl ağustos sonunda biter.
SNWS.latest: 4 Kasım 2026: Şirket 29 Ağustos 2026'da biten 52 haftanın sonuçlarını açıkladı. Hasılat 1.036,2 milyon sterlin (−%2,6). Net kâr 24,4 milyon sterlin (geçen yıl 28,3 milyon); hisse başına kâr 10,1 peni (11,7). Düşüşün nedeni tek seferlik kalemler: bu yıl 4,1 milyon sterlin yeniden yapılanma ve teknoloji gideri, geçen yıl 2,1 milyon sterlin net kazanç. Düzeltilmiş hisse başına kâr 11,3 peni (11,1). Koleksiyon ürünleri geliri %31,9 arttı; Dünya Kupası düzeltilmiş faaliyet kârına 3,5 milyon sterlin katkı yaptı. Şirket yeni sözleşmelerin yılda yaklaşık 375 milyon sterlin ek hasılat getireceğini, 2027 mali yılında ise kârlılığın kısa süreli olarak düşeceğini söyledi: 7-9 milyon sterlin geçiş gideri bekliyor. Ek net kâr beklentisi 2028'de 0-2 milyon, 2029'dan sonra yılda 12-18 milyon sterlin.
risks: Hesap büyüme varsaymıyor (yılda %0). Fiyat hesabı son 12 ayın kârına dayanıyor; şirket 2027 mali yılında kârın düşeceğini kendisi söylüyor (7-9 milyon sterlin geçiş gideri, ayrıca 21-27 milyon sterlinlik programın yarısı gider olarak yazılacak). Rakam vermediği için hesap kazancı indirmedi; marj bu yüzden olduğundan yüksek görünebilir.
Basılı gazete ve dergi satışı yapısal olarak düşüyor (şirketin varsayımı yılda %3-5). Düşüş hızlanırsa sabit maliyetli dağıtım ağının kârı hasılattan hızlı erir.

Gelir birkaç yayıncıya ve büyük perakendeciye bağlı: en büyük müşteri 125,3 milyon sterlin hasılat getiriyor. 2026 kârında Dünya Kupası koleksiyon ürünlerinin katkısı da var; bu her yıl yinelenmez.

en.one: The UK's newspaper and magazine distributor. Its equity was negative for three years; because return on equity cannot be measured, it stays at the quality wall.
en.business: Smiths News takes newspapers and magazines from publishers and delivers them every morning to more than 21,000 outlets in England and Wales. It earns a distribution margin; in each territory it is the publisher's sole wholesaler. In the fiscal year ended 29 August 2026 revenue was 1,036.2 million pounds and adjusted operating profit 38.7 million pounds. Side businesses such as collectables and waste-paper recycling are growing, but small.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The advantage comes from long, exclusive territorial contracts with publishers and from the scale of a delivery network that runs every morning. In 2026 the company extended its contracts with News UK, Telegraph, Associated Newspapers, Frontline and Seymour to 2036-2037 and won new territories; when the new contracts start it will hold about 61% of the national newspaper and magazine market. Adjusted operating profit has been level for two years (38.7 and 39.1 million pounds). The weak point: the printed newspaper market is in structural decline; newspaper revenue fell 4.1% and magazine revenue 3.2% in 2026, and the company's own long-term assumption is a fall of 3-5% a year. The profit margin is thin (about 3.7% of revenue) and depends on a few large publishers. Because equity is very small (10.7 million pounds), the real return on equity figures in the chart (880% in 2025, 230% in 2026) do not measure the quality of the business; equity was negative in earlier years.
en.mgmt: The shares are widely held; there is no controlling owner. Aberforth Partners' holding fell to 14.8% on 28 October 2026. Profit went to paying down debt and to dividends: the company reached net cash for the first time in August 2025 (bank net cash was 3.9 million pounds at the end of 2026). An ordinary dividend of 5.65 pence per share is proposed for 2026 (2025: 5.55 pence plus a 3.00 pence special dividend); there is no special dividend this year. 20.9 million pounds of dividends were paid in the year, and 5.3 million pounds of shares were bought for employee share plans. There is no buyback programme. Money now goes into the core business: the national expansion programme costs 21-27 million pounds. One problem remains from the past: the Pensions Regulator is considering a financial support direction against the company for the pension scheme of Tuffnells, which it has sold (estimated liability 3.3 million pounds; no provision made). The fiscal year ends at the end of August.
en.latest: 4 November 2026: The company announced results for the 52 weeks ended 29 August 2026. Revenue was 1,036.2 million pounds (−2.6%). Net profit was 24.4 million pounds (28.3 million a year earlier); earnings per share 10.1 pence (11.7). The fall comes from one-off items: 4.1 million pounds of reorganisation and technology costs this year, against a 2.1 million pound net credit last year. Adjusted earnings per share were 11.3 pence (11.1). Collectables revenue rose 31.9%; the World Cup added 3.5 million pounds to adjusted operating profit. The company said the new contracts will add about 375 million pounds of revenue a year, and that profitability will fall for a short time in fiscal 2027: it expects 7-9 million pounds of transition costs. It expects incremental net profit of 0-2 million pounds in 2028 and 12-18 million pounds a year from 2029.
risks: The calculation assumes no growth (0% a year). The price calculation rests on the profit of the last 12 months; the company itself says profit will fall in fiscal 2027 (7-9 million pounds of transition costs, and half of the 21-27 million pound programme will be expensed). Because it gave no figure, the calculation did not lower earnings; the margin may therefore look higher than it is.

Sales of printed newspapers and magazines are in structural decline (the company assumes 3-5% a year). If the decline speeds up, the profit of a fixed-cost delivery network shrinks faster than revenue.
Going national is a large execution task: about 700 new routes and 23 depots, with the first go-live in July 2027. Delay or cost overrun would wipe out the expected gain.
Equity is only 10.7 million pounds against total liabilities of 166.0 million pounds. An unexpected loss, or a direction over the Tuffnells pension scheme, would find no room on the balance sheet.

Revenue depends on a few publishers and large retailers: the largest customer brings 125.3 million pounds of revenue. 2026 profit also includes the contribution of World Cup collectables, which does not recur every year.
